**Kolkata**,[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-19) also known as **Calcutta**[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-20)([its official name until 2001](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_renamed_places_in_India#West_Bengal "List of renamed places in India")), is the capital and largest city of the Indian [state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/States_and_union_territories_of_India "States and union territories of India") of [West Bengal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Bengal "West Bengal"). It lies on the eastern bank of the [Hooghly River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hooghly_River "Hooghly River"), 80 km (50 mi) west of the border with [Bangladesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangladesh "Bangladesh"). It is the primary [financial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financial_centre "Financial centre") and [commercial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commercial_area "Commercial area") centre of [eastern India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_India "Eastern India") and one of the gateways to [northeastern India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northeast_India "Northeast India").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-worldbank20162-21) Kolkata is the [seventh most populous city in India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_in_India_by_population "List of cities in India by population") with an estimated [city proper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_proper "City proper") population of 4.5 million while its metropolitan region [Kolkata Metropolitan Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata_Metropolitan_Area "Kolkata Metropolitan Area") is the [third most populous metropolitan region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_million-plus_agglomerations_in_India "List of million-plus agglomerations in India") of India with a metro population of over 15 million.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-Cities1Lakhandabove-22) Kolkata is regarded by many sources as the cultural capital of India and a historically and culturally significant city in the historic [region of Bengal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengal "Bengal").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-Kolkata_Culture-1)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-23)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-24)

The three villages that predated Calcutta were ruled by the [Nawab of Bengal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nawab_of_Bengal "Nawab of Bengal") under [Mughal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mughal_emperors "Mughal emperors")[suzerainty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suzerainty "Suzerainty"). After the Nawab granted the [East India Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_India_Company "East India Company") a trading [license](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/License "License") in 1690,[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-25) the area was developed by the Company into [Fort William](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_William,_India "Fort William, India"). Nawab [Siraj ud-Daulah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siraj_ud-Daulah "Siraj ud-Daulah") occupied the fort in 1756 but was defeated at the [Battle of Plassey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Plassey "Battle of Plassey") in 1757, after his general Mir Jafar mutinied in support of the company, and was later made the Nawab for a brief time.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-26) Under [company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Company_rule_in_India "Company rule in India") and later [crown rule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crown_rule_in_India "Crown rule in India"), Calcutta served as the de facto [capital of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capital_of_India "Capital of India") until 1911. Calcutta was the second largest city in the [British Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Empire "British Empire"), after [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London"),[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-27) and was the centre of bureaucracy, politics, law, education, science and [the arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_arts "The arts") in India. The city was associated with many of the figures and movements of the [Bengali Renaissance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengali_Renaissance "Bengali Renaissance"). It was the hotbed of the [Indian nationalist movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_nationalist_movement "Indian nationalist movement").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-28)

The [partition of Bengal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partition_of_Bengal_(1947) "Partition of Bengal (1947)") in 1947 affected the fortunes of the city. Following independence in 1947, Kolkata, which was once the premier centre of Indian commerce, culture, and politics, suffered many decades of [political violence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_violence "Political violence") and [economic stagnation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_stagnation "Economic stagnation") before it rebounded.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-ianjack-29) In the late 20th century, the city hosted the [government-in-exile of Bangladesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Provisional_Government_of_Bangladesh "Provisional Government of Bangladesh") during the [Bangladesh Liberation War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangladesh_Liberation_War "Bangladesh Liberation War") in 1971.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-auto-30) It was also flooded with Hindu [refugees from East Bengal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Bengali_refugees "East Bengali refugees") (present-day Bangladesh) in the decades following the 1947 [partition of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partition_of_India "Partition of India"), transforming its landscape and shaping its politics.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-31)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-32) The city was overtaken by [Mumbai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumbai "Mumbai") (formerly Bombay) as India's largest city.

A demographically diverse city, the [culture of Kolkata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Culture_of_Kolkata "Culture of Kolkata") features idiosyncrasies that include distinctively [close-knit neighbourhoods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Para_(Bengali) "Para (Bengali)") (_paras_) and [freestyle conversations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adda_(South_Asian) "Adda (South Asian)") (_adda_). Kolkata's architecture includes many imperial landmarks, including the [Victoria Memorial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria_Memorial,_Kolkata "Victoria Memorial, Kolkata"), [Howrah Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Howrah_Bridge "Howrah Bridge") and the [Grand Hotel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oberoi_Grand "Oberoi Grand"). The city's heritage includes India's only [Chinatown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinatown,_Kolkata "Chinatown, Kolkata") and remnants of [Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_Jews_in_Kolkata "History of the Jews in Kolkata"), Armenian, Greek and Anglo-Indian communities. The city is closely linked with [Bhadralok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhadralok "Bhadralok") culture and the [Zamindars of Bengal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zamindars_of_Bengal "Zamindars of Bengal"), including [Bengali Hindu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengali_Hindu "Bengali Hindu"), [Bengali Muslim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengali_Muslim "Bengali Muslim") and tribal aristocrats. The city is often regarded as India's cultural capital.

Kolkata is home to institutions of national importance, including the [Academy of Fine Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_of_Fine_Arts,_Kolkata "Academy of Fine Arts, Kolkata"), the [Asiatic Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Asiatic_Society "The Asiatic Society"), the [Indian Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Museum "Indian Museum") and the [National Library of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Library_of_India "National Library of India"). The [University of Calcutta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Calcutta "University of Calcutta"), the first modern university in South Asia, and its affiliated colleges produced many leading figures of South Asia. It is the centre of the Indian Bengali film industry, which is known as [Tollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinema_of_West_Bengal "Cinema of West Bengal"). Among scientific institutions, Kolkata hosts the [Geological Survey of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geological_Survey_of_India "Geological Survey of India"), the [Botanical Survey of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Botanical_Survey_of_India "Botanical Survey of India"), the [Calcutta Mathematical Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta_Mathematical_Society "Calcutta Mathematical Society"), the [Indian Science Congress Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Science_Congress_Association "Indian Science Congress Association"), the [Zoological Survey of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zoological_Survey_of_India "Zoological Survey of India"), the [Horticultural Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agri_Horticultural_Society_of_India "Agri Horticultural Society of India"), the [Institution of Engineers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Institution_of_Engineers_(India) "Institution of Engineers (India)"), the [Anthropological Survey of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthropological_Survey_of_India "Anthropological Survey of India") and the Indian Public Health Association. The [Port of Kolkata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_of_Kolkata "Port of Kolkata") is India's oldest operating port. Four Nobel laureates and two Nobel Memorial Prize winners are associated with the city.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-Kolkata_Nobel-33) Though home to major cricketing venues and franchises, Kolkata stands out in India for being the country's centre of association football. Kolkata is known for its grand celebrations of the Hindu festival of [Durga Puja](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Durga_Puja "Durga Puja"), which is recognized by UNESCO for its importance to world heritage.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-finds-34) Kolkata is also known as the _''City of Joy''_.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-indiatimes-35)

## Etymology

Main article: [Etymology of Kolkata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Etymology_of_Kolkata "Etymology of Kolkata")

The word _Kolkata_ ([Bengali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengali_language "Bengali language"): কলকাতা[[kolˈkata]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Bengali "Help:IPA/Bengali")) derives from _[Kôlikata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalikata "Kalikata")_ (Bengali: কলিকাতা[[ˈkɔliˌkata]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Bengali "Help:IPA/Bengali")), the Bengali language name of one of three villages that predated the arrival of the British; the other two villages were [Sutanuti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sutanuti "Sutanuti") and [Govindapur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gobindapur,_Kolkata "Gobindapur, Kolkata").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-spatialchange-36)

There are several explanations for the etymology of this name:

*   _Kolikata_ is thought to be a variation of _Kalikkhetrô_ ([Bengali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengali_language "Bengali language"): কালীক্ষেত্র[[ˈkaliˌkʰetrɔ]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Bengali "Help:IPA/Bengali")), meaning 'Field of [the goddess] [Kali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kali "Kali")'. Similarly, it can be a variation of _Kalikshetra_ ([Sanskrit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanskrit "Sanskrit"): कालीक्षेत्र, lit. 'area of Goddess Kali').
*   Another theory is that the name derives from [Kalighat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalighat "Kalighat").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-37)
*   Alternatively, the name may have been derived from the Bengali term _kilkila_ ([Bengali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengali_language "Bengali language"): কিলকিলা), or 'flat area'.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-chatterjeename-38)
*   The name may have its origin in the words _khal_ ([Bengali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengali_language "Bengali language"): খাল[[ˈkʰal]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Bengali "Help:IPA/Bengali")) meaning 'canal', followed by _kaṭa_ ([Bengali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengali_language "Bengali language"): কাটা[[ˈkaʈa]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Bengali "Help:IPA/Bengali")), which may mean 'dug'.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-Nair-39)
*   According to another theory, the area specialised in the production of [quicklime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcium_oxide "Calcium oxide") or _koli chun_ ([Bengali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengali_language "Bengali language"): কলি চুন[[ˈkɔliˌtʃun]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Bengali "Help:IPA/Bengali")) and coir or _kata_ ([Bengali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengali_language "Bengali language"): কাতা[[ˈkata]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Bengali "Help:IPA/Bengali")); hence, it was called _Kolikata_).[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-chatterjeename-38)

Although the city's name has always been pronounced _Kolkata_ or _Kôlikata_ in Bengali, the anglicised form _Calcutta_ was the official name until 2001, when it [was changed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renaming_of_cities_in_India "Renaming of cities in India") to _Kolkata_ to match Bengali pronunciation.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-40) Both English variants are used.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-longman-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-MB-18)

## History

Main article: [History of Kolkata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Kolkata "History of Kolkata")

[![Image 30](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8c/Fort_William%2C_Calcutta%2C_1735.jpg/250px-Fort_William%2C_Calcutta%2C_1735.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Fort_William,_Calcutta,_1735.jpg)

Ships of the [British East India Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_East_India_Company "British East India Company") near [Fort William](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_William,_India "Fort William, India") in the [Port of Calcutta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_of_Calcutta "Port of Calcutta") in 1735

The discovery and [archaeological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archaeological "Archaeological") study of [Chandraketugarh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chandraketugarh "Chandraketugarh"), 35 km (22 mi) north of Kolkata, provide evidence that the region in which the city stands has been inhabited for over two millennia.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-41)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-Das-42) Kolkata or Kalikata in its earliest mentions, is described to be a village surrounded with jungle on the bank of river Ganga as a renowned port, commercial hub and a Hindu pilgrimage site for [Kalighat Temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalighat_Kali_Temple "Kalighat Kali Temple"). The first mention of the Kalikata village was found in [Bipradas Pipilai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bipradas_Pipilai "Bipradas Pipilai")'s _Manasa Vijay_ (1495), where he describes how [Chand Sadagar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chand_Sadagar "Chand Sadagar") used to stop in Kalighat to worship [Goddess Kali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kali "Kali") during his path to trade voyage.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-43)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-:_Radharaman-44) Later Kalikata was also found to be mentioned in [Mukundaram Chakrabarti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mukundaram_Chakrabarti "Mukundaram Chakrabarti")'s _[Chandimangal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chandimangal "Chandimangal")_ (1594), [Todar Mal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Todar_Mal "Todar Mal")'s taxation-list in 1596 and Krishnaram Das's _Kalikamangal_ (1676–77).[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-:_Radharaman-44)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-45) Kalighat was then considered a safe place for businessmen. They used to carry on trade through the Bhagirathi and took shelter there at night.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-:0-46) Kolkata's [recorded history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recorded_history "Recorded history") began in 1690 with the arrival of the English [East India Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_India_Company "East India Company"), which was consolidating its trade business in Bengal. [Job Charnock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Job_Charnock "Job Charnock") is often regarded as the founder of the city;[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-47) however, in response to a public petition,[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-48) the [Calcutta High Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta_High_Court "Calcutta High Court") ruled in 2003 that the city does not have a founder.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-notcharnock-49) The area occupied by the present-day city encompassed three villages: [Kalikata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalikata "Kalikata"), [Gobindapur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gobindapur,_Kolkata "Gobindapur, Kolkata") and [Sutanuti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sutanuti "Sutanuti"). Kalikata was a fishing village, where a handful of merchants began their operations by building a factory;[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-:0-46) Sutanuti was a riverside weavers' village; and Gobindapur was a trading post for Indian merchant princes. These villages were part of an estate belonging to the [Sabarna Roy Choudhury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabarna_Roy_Choudhury "Sabarna Roy Choudhury") family of _[zamindars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zamindar "Zamindar")_. The estate was sold to the East India Company in 1698.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-BanerjeePage1and3-50):1

In 1712, the British completed the construction of [Fort William](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_William,_India "Fort William, India"), located on the east bank of the Hooghly River to protect their trading factory.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-mitter-51) Facing frequent skirmishes with [French forces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Indies_Company "French Indies Company"), the British began to upgrade their fortifications in 1756. The Nawab of Bengal, [Siraj-ud-Daulah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siraj_ud-Daulah "Siraj ud-Daulah"), condemned the militarisation and tax evasion by the company. His warning went unheeded, and the Nawab attacked; his capture of Fort William led to the killings of several East India company officials in the [Black Hole of Calcutta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Hole_of_Calcutta "Black Hole of Calcutta").[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-hunterhistory-52) A force of Company soldiers (_[sepoys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sepoy "Sepoy")_) and British troops led by [Robert Clive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Clive "Robert Clive") recaptured the city the following year.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-hunterhistory-52) Per the 1765 [Treaty of Allahabad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Allahabad "Treaty of Allahabad") following the [battle of Buxar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Buxar "Battle of Buxar"), East India company was appointed imperial tax collector of the Mughal emperor in the province of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa, while Mughal-appointed Nawabs continued to rule the province.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-AhmedFarooqui-53) Declared a [presidency city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidencies_and_provinces_of_British_India "Presidencies and provinces of British India"), Calcutta became the headquarters of the East India Company by 1773.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-Arnold-Baker2015-54)

In 1793, ruling power of the Nawabs were abolished, and East India company took complete control of the city and the province. In the early 19th century, the marshes surrounding the city were drained; the government area was laid out along the banks of the Hooghly River. [Richard Wellesley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Wellesley,_1st_Marquess_Wellesley "Richard Wellesley, 1st Marquess Wellesley"), [Governor-General of the Presidency of Fort William](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor-General_of_the_Presidency_of_Fort_William "Governor-General of the Presidency of Fort William") between 1797 and 1805, was largely responsible for the development of the city and its public architecture.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-55) Throughout the late 18th and 19th century, the city was a centre of the East India Company's opium trade.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-56) A census in 1837 records the population of the city proper as 229,700, of which the British residents made up only 3,138.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-57) The same source says another 177,000 resided in the suburbs and neighbouring villages, making the entire population of greater Calcutta 406,700.

Bengali billboards in 1945

In 1864, a typhoon struck the city and killed about 60,000 in Kolkata.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-58)

By the 1850s, Calcutta had two areas: White Town, which was primarily British and centred on [Chowringhee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chowringhee "Chowringhee") and [Dalhousie Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalhousie_Square "Dalhousie Square"); and Black Town, mainly Indian and centred on North Calcutta.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-hardgrave-59) The city underwent rapid industrial growth starting in the early 1850s, especially in the textile and jute industries; this encouraged British companies to massively invest in infrastructure projects, which included telegraph connections and [Howrah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Howrah_railway_station "Howrah railway station"). The coalescence of British and Indian culture resulted in the emergence of a new _[babu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Babu\_(title) "Babu (title)")_ class of urbane Indians, whose members were often bureaucrats, professionals, newspaper readers, and Anglophiles; they usually belonged to upper-caste Hindu communities.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-60) In the 19th century, the [Bengal Renaissance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengal_Renaissance "Bengal Renaissance") brought about an increased sociocultural sophistication among city denizens. In 1883, Calcutta was host to the first national conference of the [Indian National Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_National_Association "Indian National Association"), which was the first avowed nationalist organisation in India.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-stepienchap3-61)

The [partition of Bengal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partition_of_Bengal_(1905) "Partition of Bengal (1905)") in 1905 along religious lines led to mass protests, making Calcutta a less hospitable place for the British.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-62)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-63) The capital was moved to New Delhi in 1911.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-64) Calcutta continued to be a centre for [revolutionary organisations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revolutionary_movement_for_Indian_independence "Revolutionary movement for Indian independence") associated with the [Indian independence movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_independence_movement "Indian independence movement"). The city and its port were bombed several times by the [Japanese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imperial_Japanese_Army "Imperial Japanese Army") between 1942 and 1944, during [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II").[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-Randhawa-65)[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-PacificWar-66) Millions starved to death during the [Bengal famine of 1943](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengal_famine_of_1943 "Bengal famine of 1943") (at the same time of the war) due to a combination of military, administrative, and natural factors.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-67)[Demands for the creation of a Muslim state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakistan_Movement "Pakistan Movement") led in 1946 to [an episode of communal violence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Direct_Action_Day "Direct Action Day") that killed over 4,000.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-Burrows-68)[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-DasS-69)[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-Talukdar-70) The [partition of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partition_of_India "Partition of India") led to further clashes and a demographic shift—many Muslims left for [East Bengal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Bengal "East Bengal") (later [East Pakistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Pakistan "East Pakistan"), present day [Bangladesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangladesh "Bangladesh")), while hundreds of thousands of Hindus fled into the city.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-71)

During the 1960s and 1970s, severe power shortages, strikes and a violent [Marxist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marxist "Marxist")–[Maoist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maoist "Maoist") movement by groups known as the [Naxalites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naxalite "Naxalite") damaged much of the city's infrastructure, resulting in economic stagnation.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-ianjack-29) During East Pakistan's secessionist [war of independence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangladesh_Liberation_War "Bangladesh Liberation War") in 1971, the city was home to the [government-in-exile of Bangladesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Provisional_Government_of_Bangladesh "Provisional Government of Bangladesh").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-auto-30) During the war, refugees poured into West Bengal and strained Kolkata's infrastructure.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-72) The [Eastern Command](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Command_(India) "Eastern Command (India)") of the Indian military, which is based in Fort William, played a pivotal role in the [Indo-Pakistani war of 1971](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indo-Pakistani_war_of_1971 "Indo-Pakistani war of 1971") and securing the [surrender of Pakistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surrender_of_Pakistan "Surrender of Pakistan"). During the mid-1980s, [Mumbai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumbai "Mumbai") (then called Bombay) overtook Kolkata as India's most populous city. In 1985, Prime Minister [Rajiv Gandhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajiv_Gandhi "Rajiv Gandhi") dubbed Kolkata a "dying city" in light of its socio-political woes.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-73) In the period 1977–2011, West Bengal was governed from Kolkata by the [Left Front](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Left_Front_(West_Bengal) "Left Front (West Bengal)"), which was dominated by the [Communist Party of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_Party_of_India_(Marxist) "Communist Party of India (Marxist)") (CPM). It was the world's longest-serving democratically elected communist government, during which Kolkata was a key base for [Indian communism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Socialism_in_India "Socialism in India").[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-Biswas-74)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-75)[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-76) The city's economic recovery gathered momentum after the 1990s, when [India began to institute pro-market reforms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_liberalisation_in_India "Economic liberalisation in India"). Since 2000, the information technology (IT) services sector has revitalised Kolkata's stagnant economy. The city is also experiencing marked growth in its manufacturing base. In the [2011 West Bengal Legislative Assembly election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_West_Bengal_Legislative_Assembly_election "2011 West Bengal Legislative Assembly election"), Left Front was succeeded by the [Trinamool Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trinamool_Congress "Trinamool Congress").[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-bbceco-77)

## Geography

Main article: [Geography of Kolkata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geography_of_Kolkata "Geography of Kolkata")

[![Image 33](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a1/Earth_from_Space-_Kolkata%2C_India_ESA24701909.jpeg/250px-Earth_from_Space-_Kolkata%2C_India_ESA24701909.jpeg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Earth_from_Space-_Kolkata,_India_ESA24701909.jpeg)

Kolkata from space, captured by Copernicus [Sentinel-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sentinel-2 "Sentinel-2")

Spread roughly meridionally along the east bank of the [Hooghly River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hooghly_River "Hooghly River"), Kolkata sits within the lower [Ganges Delta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ganges_Delta "Ganges Delta") of eastern India approximately 75 km (47 mi) west of the international border with Bangladesh; the city's elevation is 1.5–9 m (5–30 ft).[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-78) Much of the city was originally a wetland that was reclaimed over the decades to accommodate a burgeoning population.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-79) The remaining undeveloped areas, known as the [East Kolkata Wetlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Kolkata_Wetlands "East Kolkata Wetlands"), were designated a "wetland of international importance" by the [Ramsar Convention](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramsar_Convention "Ramsar Convention") (1975).[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-80) As with most of the [Indo-Gangetic Plain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indo-Gangetic_Plain "Indo-Gangetic Plain"), the soil and water are predominantly [alluvial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alluvium "Alluvium") in origin. Kolkata is located over the "Bengal basin", a pericratonic tertiary basin.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-soil_characterisation-81)

The Bengal basin comprises three structural units: shelf or platform in the west; central hinge or shelf/slope break; and deep basinal part in the east and southeast. Kolkata is located atop the western part of the hinge zone which is about 25 km (16 mi) wide at a depth of about 45,000 m (148,000 ft) below the surface.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-soil_characterisation-81) The shelf and hinge zones have many faults, among them some are active. Total thickness of sediment below Kolkata is nearly 7,500 m (24,600 ft) above the [crystalline basement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basement_(geology) "Basement (geology)"); of these the top 350–450 m (1,150–1,480 ft) is [Quaternary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quaternary "Quaternary"), followed by 4,500–5,500 m (14,760–18,040 ft) of [Tertiary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tertiary_(period) "Tertiary (period)") sediments, 500–700 m (1,640–2,300 ft)[trap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trap_rock "Trap rock") wash of [Cretaceous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cretaceous "Cretaceous") trap and 600–800 m (1,970–2,620 ft)[Permian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Permian "Permian")-[Carboniferous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carboniferous "Carboniferous")[Gondwana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gondwana "Gondwana") rocks.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-soil_characterisation-81) The quaternary sediments consist of clay, silt and several grades of sand and gravel. These sediments are sandwiched between two clay beds: the lower one at a depth of 250–650 m (820–2,130 ft); the upper one 10–40 m (30–130 ft) in thickness.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-Bunting-82) According to the [Bureau of Indian Standards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bureau_of_Indian_Standards "Bureau of Indian Standards"), on a scale ranging from I to V in order of increasing susceptibility to earthquakes, the city lies inside [seismic zone III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earthquake_hazard_zoning_of_India "Earthquake hazard zoning of India").[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-hazardprofile-83)

### Climate

Main article: [Climate of Kolkata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate_of_Kolkata "Climate of Kolkata")

According to a [United Nations Development Programme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Development_Programme "United Nations Development Programme") report, its wind and cyclone zone is "very high damage risk".[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-hazardprofile-83)

#### Temperature

The annual mean temperature is 26.8°C (80.2°F); monthly mean temperatures are 19–30°C (66–86°F). Summers (March–June) are hot and humid, with temperatures in the low 30s Celsius; during dry spells, maximum temperatures sometime exceed 40°C (104°F) in May and June.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-weatherbase-92) Winter lasts for roughly 2+1⁄2 months, with seasonal lows dipping to 9–11°C (48–52°F) in December and January. May is the hottest month, with daily temperatures ranging from 27–37°C (81–99°F); January, the coldest month, has temperatures varying from 12–23°C (54–73°F). The highest recorded temperature is 43.9°C (111.0°F), and the lowest is 5°C (41°F).[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-weatherbase-92) The winter is mild and very comfortable weather pertains over the city throughout this season. Often, in April–June, the city is struck by heavy rains or dusty squalls that are followed by thunderstorms or hailstorms, bringing cooling relief from the prevailing humidity. These thunderstorms are [convective](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convection_rain "Convection rain") in nature, and are known locally as _kal bôishakhi_ (কালবৈশাখী), or "Nor'westers" in English.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-kalboisakhi-93)

#### Rainfall

Rains brought by the Bay of Bengal branch of the [south-west summer monsoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southwest_monsoon "Southwest monsoon")[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-monsoontribune-94) lash Kolkata between June and September, supplying it with most of its annual rainfall of about 1,850 mm (73 in). The highest monthly rainfall total occurs in July and August. In these months often incessant rain for days brings life to a stall for the city dwellers. The city receives 2,107 hours of sunshine per year, with maximum [sunlight exposure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insolation "Insolation") occurring in April.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-ESS-95) Kolkata has been hit by several cyclones; these include systems occurring in [1737](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1737_Calcutta_cyclone "1737 Calcutta cyclone") and [1864](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1864_Calcutta_cyclone "1864 Calcutta cyclone") that killed thousands.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-96)[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-97) More recently, [Cyclone Aila](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyclone_Aila "Cyclone Aila") in 2009 and [Cyclone Amphan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyclone_Amphan "Cyclone Amphan") in 2020 caused widespread damage to Kolkata by bringing catastrophic winds and torrential rainfall.

### Environmental issues

Main article: [Environmental issues in Kolkata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Environmental_issues_in_Kolkata "Environmental issues in Kolkata")

Pollution is a major concern in Kolkata. As of 2008[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kolkata&action=edit), [sulfur dioxide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sulfur_dioxide "Sulfur dioxide") and [nitrogen dioxide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nitrogen_dioxide "Nitrogen dioxide") annual concentration were within the national ambient air quality standards of India, but respirable [suspended particulate matter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Particulates "Particulates") levels were high, and on an increasing trend for five consecutive years, causing smog and haze.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-ambientairquality-98)[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-99) Severe air pollution in the city has caused a rise in pollution-related respiratory ailments, such as lung cancer.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-BBC51707-100)

## Cityscape and urban structure

[![Image 34](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/21/Chowringheeskyline2.jpg/500px-Chowringheeskyline2.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Chowringheeskyline2.jpg)

Kolkata's cityscape

Kolkata, which is under the jurisdiction of the [Kolkata Municipal Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata_Municipal_Corporation "Kolkata Municipal Corporation") (KMC), has an area of 206.08 km 2 (80 sq mi).[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-Metropolis-101) The east–west dimension of the city is comparatively narrow, stretching from the Hooghly River in the west to roughly the [Eastern Metropolitan Bypass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Metropolitan_Bypass "Eastern Metropolitan Bypass") in the east—a span of 9–10 km (5.6–6.2 mi).[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-102) The north–south distance is greater, and its axis is used to section the city into North, Central, South and East Kolkata. North Kolkata is the oldest part of the city. Characterised by 19th-century architecture and narrow alleyways, it includes areas such as [Jorasanko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jorasanko "Jorasanko"), [Rajabazar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajabazar,_Kolkata "Rajabazar, Kolkata"), [Maniktala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maniktala "Maniktala"), [Ultadanga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ultadanga "Ultadanga"), [Shyambazar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shyambazar "Shyambazar"), [Shobhabazar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shobhabazar "Shobhabazar"), [Bagbazar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bagbazar "Bagbazar"), [Cossipore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cossipore "Cossipore"), [Sinthee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinthee "Sinthee") etc. The north suburban areas like [Dum Dum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dum_Dum "Dum Dum"), [Baranagar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baranagar "Baranagar"), [Belgharia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgharia "Belgharia"), [Sodepur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sodepur "Sodepur"), [Khardaha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khardaha "Khardaha"), [New Barrackpore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Barrackpore "New Barrackpore"), [Madhyamgram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhyamgram "Madhyamgram"), [Barrackpore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barrackpore "Barrackpore"), [Barasat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barasat "Barasat") etc. are also within the city of Kolkata (as a metropolitan structure).[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-urbanprice-103):65–66

Central Kolkata hosts the central business district. It contains [B. B. D. Bagh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B._B._D._Bagh "B. B. D. Bagh"), formerly known as Dalhousie Square, and the [Esplanade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Esplanade,_Kolkata "Esplanade, Kolkata") on its east; [Rajiv Gandhi Sarani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strand_Road,_Kolkata "Strand Road, Kolkata") is on its west.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-104) The [West Bengal Secretariat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Writers'_Building "Writers' Building"), [General Post Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Post_Office,_Kolkata "General Post Office, Kolkata"), [Reserve Bank of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reserve_Bank_of_India "Reserve Bank of India"), [Calcutta High Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta_High_Court "Calcutta High Court"), [Lalbazar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lalbazar "Lalbazar") Police Headquarters and several other government and private offices are located there. Another business hub is the area south of [Park Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Street,_Kolkata "Park Street, Kolkata"), which comprises thoroughfares such as [Jawahar Lal Nehru Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chowringhee_Road "Chowringhee Road"), [Abanindranath Thakur Sarani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abanindranath_Thakur_Sarani "Abanindranath Thakur Sarani"), Dr. Martin Luther King Sarani, Dr. Upendra Nath Brahmachari Sarani, [Shakespeare Sarani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shakespeare_Sarani "Shakespeare Sarani") and [Acharay Jagadish Chandra Basu Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AJC_Bose_Road "AJC Bose Road").[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-105)

[![Image 35](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f6/Park_street_area_kolkata_2020.jpg/250px-Park_street_area_kolkata_2020.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Park_street_area_kolkata_2020.jpg)

[Park Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Street,_Kolkata "Park Street, Kolkata"), one of the upmarket areas in Kolkata

South Kolkata developed after India gained independence in 1947; it includes upscale neighbourhoods such as [Bhowanipore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhowanipore "Bhowanipore"), [Alipore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alipore "Alipore"), [Ballygunge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ballygunge "Ballygunge"), [Kasba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kasba,_Kolkata "Kasba, Kolkata"), [Dhakuria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhakuria "Dhakuria"), [Santoshpur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santoshpur,_Kolkata "Santoshpur, Kolkata"), [Garia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garia "Garia"), [Golf Green](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golf_Green "Golf Green"), [Tollygunge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tollygunge "Tollygunge"), [New Alipore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Alipore "New Alipore"), [Behala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Behala "Behala"), [Barisha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barisha,_Kolkata "Barisha, Kolkata") etc. The south suburban areas like [Maheshtala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maheshtala "Maheshtala"), [Budge Budge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Budge_Budge "Budge Budge"), [Rajpur Sonarpur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajpur_Sonarpur "Rajpur Sonarpur"), [Baruipur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baruipur "Baruipur") etc. are also within the city of Kolkata (as a metropolitan structure).[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-spatialchange-36) The [Maidan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maidan_(Kolkata) "Maidan (Kolkata)") is a large open field in the heart of the city that has been called the "lungs of Kolkata"[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-106) and accommodates sporting events and public meetings.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-107) The [Victoria Memorial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria_Memorial,_Kolkata "Victoria Memorial, Kolkata") and [Kolkata Race Course](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata_Race_Course "Kolkata Race Course") are located at the southern end of the Maidan. Among the other parks are [Central Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Park_(Kolkata) "Central Park (Kolkata)") in Bidhannagar and [Millennium Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millennium_Park_(Kolkata) "Millennium Park (Kolkata)") on Rajiv Gandhi Sarani, along the Hooghly River.

### Metropolitan area and satellite cities

The [Kolkata metropolitan area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata_metropolitan_area "Kolkata metropolitan area") is spread over 1,886.67 km 2 (728.45 sq mi)[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-kmdaanreport2011kma-108):7 and comprises 4 municipal corporations (including Kolkata Municipal Corporation), 37[local municipalities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neighbourhoods_in_Kolkata "Neighbourhoods in Kolkata") and 24[panchayat samitis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panchayat_samiti "Panchayat samiti"), as of 2011[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kolkata&action=edit).[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-kmdaanreport2011kma-108):7 The urban agglomeration encompassed 72 cities and 527 towns and villages, as of 2006[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kolkata&action=edit).[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-Metropolis-101) Suburban areas in the Kolkata metropolitan area incorporate parts of the following districts: [North 24 Parganas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_24_Parganas_district "North 24 Parganas district"), [South 24 Parganas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_24_Parganas_district "South 24 Parganas district"), [Howrah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Howrah_district "Howrah district"), [Hooghly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hooghly_district "Hooghly district") and [Nadia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nadia_district "Nadia district").[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-urbanprice-103):15

[![Image 36](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3e/Kolkata_Gate_%28officially_known_as_Biswa_Bangla_Gate%29.jpg/250px-Kolkata_Gate_%28officially_known_as_Biswa_Bangla_Gate%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kolkata_Gate_(officially_known_as_Biswa_Bangla_Gate).jpg)

[Biswa Bangla Gate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biswa_Bangla_Gate "Biswa Bangla Gate") in [New Town, Kolkata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Town,_Kolkata "New Town, Kolkata")

Two planned townships in the greater Kolkata region are [Bidhannagar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bidhannagar,_Kolkata "Bidhannagar, Kolkata"), also known as Salt Lake City and located north-east of the city; and [Rajarhat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajarhat "Rajarhat"), also called [New Town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Town,_Kolkata "New Town, Kolkata") and located east of Bidhannagar.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-spatialchange-36)[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-Sectorv-109) In the 2000s, Sector 5 in Bidhannagar developed into a business hub for information technology and telecommunication companies.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-110)[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-111) Both Bidhannagar and New Town are situated outside the Kolkata Municipal Corporation limits, in their own municipal corporations or authorities.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-Sectorv-109)

## Economy

Main article: [Economy of Kolkata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economy_of_Kolkata "Economy of Kolkata")

[![Image 37](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/93/Tata_Centre_-_43_Chowringhee_Road_-_Kolkata_2013-01-05_2429.JPG/250px-Tata_Centre_-_43_Chowringhee_Road_-_Kolkata_2013-01-05_2429.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Tata_Centre_-_43_Chowringhee_Road_-_Kolkata_2013-01-05_2429.JPG)

[Tata Steel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tata_Steel "Tata Steel") building in Kolkata [CBD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Business_District "Central Business District")

[![Image 38](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/51/Kolkata_skyline_at_night.jpg/330px-Kolkata_skyline_at_night.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kolkata_skyline_at_night.jpg)

Kolkata old CBD skyline consisting of [SBI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_Bank_of_India "State Bank of India") Eastern HQ and [GoWB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_West_Bengal "Government of West Bengal") New Secretariat Building

Kolkata is the commercial and financial hub of [East](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_India "East India") and [Northeast India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northeast_India "Northeast India")[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-urbanprice-103) and home to the [Calcutta Stock Exchange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta_Stock_Exchange "Calcutta Stock Exchange").[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-CSE-112)[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-worldbank2016-113) It is a major commercial and military port, and is one of five cities in eastern India (alongside [Bhubaneswar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biju_Patnaik_Airport "Biju Patnaik Airport"), [Guwahati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lokpriya_Gopinath_Bordoloi_International_Airport "Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport"), [Imphal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imphal_Airport "Imphal Airport"), and [Kushinagar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kushinagar_International_Airport "Kushinagar International Airport")) to have an international airport. Once India's leading city, Kolkata experienced a steady economic decline in the decades following India's independence due to steep population increases and a rise in militant [trade-unionism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trade-unionism "Trade-unionism"), which included frequent strikes that were backed by left-wing parties.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-bbceco-77) From the 1960s to the late 1990s, several factories were closed and businesses relocated.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-bbceco-77) The lack of capital and resources added to the depressed state of the city's economy and gave rise to an unwelcome sobriquet: the "dying city".[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-114) The city's fortunes improved after the [Indian economy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economy_of_India "Economy of India") was liberalised in the 1990s and changes in economic policy were enacted by the West Bengal state government.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-bbceco-77) Recent estimates of the economy of Kolkata's metropolitan area have ranged from $150 to$250 billion ([PPP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Purchasing_power_parity "Purchasing power parity") GDP), and have ranked it [Fourth-most productive metro area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_by_GDP "List of cities by GDP") of India.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-gdp-115)

Flexible production has been the norm in Kolkata, which has an [informal sector](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Informal_sector "Informal sector") that employs more than 40% of the labour force.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-spatialchange-36) One unorganised group, [roadside hawkers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawkers_in_Kolkata "Hawkers in Kolkata"), generated business worth ₹87.72 billion (equivalent to ₹330 billion or US$3.4 billion in 2026) in 2005.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-Telegraphhawker-116)As of 2001[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kolkata&action=edit), around 0.81% of the city's workforce was employed in the [primary sector](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primary_sector_of_the_economy "Primary sector of the economy") (agriculture, forestry, mining, etc.); 15.49% worked in the [secondary sector](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secondary_sector_of_the_economy "Secondary sector of the economy") (industrial and manufacturing); and 83.69% worked in the [tertiary sector](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tertiary_sector_of_the_economy "Tertiary sector of the economy") (service industries).[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-urbanprice-103):19 As of 2003[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kolkata&action=edit), the majority of households in slums were engaged in occupations belonging to the informal sector; 36.5% were involved in servicing the urban middle class (as maids, drivers, etc.) and 22.2% were [casual labourers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wage_labour "Wage labour").[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-kundu-117):11 About 34% of the available labour force in Kolkata slums were unemployed.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-kundu-117):11 According to one estimate, almost a quarter of the population live on less than ₹27 (28¢US) per day.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-2014_Indian_general_election,_Calcutta-118)

Major manufacturing companies in the city are [Alstom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alstom "Alstom"), [Larsen & Toubro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larsen_&_Toubro "Larsen & Toubro"),[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-119)[Fosroc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fosroc "Fosroc"),[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-120)[Videocon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Videocon_Telecom "Videocon Telecom").[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-121) As in many other Indian cities, information technology became a high-growth sector in Kolkata starting in the late 1990s; the city's IT sector grew at 70% per annum—a rate that was twice the national average.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-bbceco-77) The 2000s saw a surge of investments in the real estate, infrastructure, retail, and hospitality sectors; [several large shopping malls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_shopping_malls_in_Kolkata "List of shopping malls in Kolkata") and hotels were launched.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-122)[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-123)[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-124)[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-125)[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-126) Companies such as [ITC Limited](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITC_Limited "ITC Limited"), [CESC Limited](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CESC_Limited "CESC Limited"), [Exide Industries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exide_Industries "Exide Industries"), [Emami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emami "Emami"), [Eveready Industries India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eveready_Industries_India "Eveready Industries India"), [Lux Industries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lux_Industries "Lux Industries"), [Rupa Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rupa_Company "Rupa Company"), [Berger Paints](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berger_Paints "Berger Paints"), [Birla Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birla_Corporation "Birla Corporation"), [Britannia Industries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Britannia_Industries "Britannia Industries") and [Purushottam Publishers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Purushottam_Publishers "Purushottam Publishers")[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta#cite_note-127) are headquartered in the city. [Philips](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philips "Philips") India, [PwC India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PwC_India "PwC India"), [Tata Global Beverages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tata_Global_Beverages "Tata Global Beverages"), and [Tata Steel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tata_Steel "Tata Steel") have their registered office and zonal headquarters in Kolkata. Kolkata hosts the headquarters of two major banks: [UCO Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UCO_Bank "UCO Bank"), and [Bandhan Bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bandhan_Bank "Bandhan Bank"). [Reserve Bank of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reserve_Bank_of_India "Reserve Bank of India"), [State Bank of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_Bank_of_India "State Bank of India") have its eastern zonal office in Kolkata. [India Government Mint, Kolkata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India_Government_Mint,_Kolkata "India Government Mint, Kolkata") is one of the four mints in India. Some of the oldest public sector companies are headquartered in the city such as the [Coal India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coal_India "Coal India"), [National Insurance Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Insurance_Company "National Insurance Company"), [Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garden_Reach_Shipbuilders_&_Engineers "Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers"), [Tea Board of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tea_Board_of_India "Tea Board of India"), [Geological Survey of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geological_Survey_of_India "Geological Survey of India"), [Zoological Survey of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zoological_Survey_of_India "Zoological Survey of India"), [Botanical Survey of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Botanical_Survey_of_India "Botanical Survey of India"), [Jute Corporation of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jute_Corporation_of_India "Jute Corporation of India"), National Test House, [Hindustan Copper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindustan_Copper?action=edit&redlink=1 "Hindustan Copper (page does not exist)") and the [Ordnance Factories Board](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ordnance_Factories_Board "Ordnance Factories Board") of the [Indian Ministry of Defence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Defence_(India) "Ministry of Defence (India)").

The **Bengal Presidency**, officially the **Presidency of Fort William in Bengal** until 1937, later the **Bengal Province**, was the largest of all three [presidencies of British India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidencies_of_British_India "Presidencies of British India") during [Company rule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Company_rule_in_India "Company rule in India") and later a [province of British Raj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Provinces_of_India "Provinces of India").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengal_Presidency#cite_note-7) At the height of its territorial jurisdiction, it covered large parts of what is now South Asia and Southeast Asia. Bengal proper covered the ethno-linguistic region of [Bengal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengal "Bengal") (present-day [Bangladesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangladesh "Bangladesh") and the Indian state of [West Bengal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Bengal "West Bengal")). [Calcutta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta "Calcutta"), the city which grew around [Fort William](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_William,_India "Fort William, India"), was the capital of the Bengal Presidency. For many years, the [governor of Bengal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_Bengal "Governor of Bengal") was concurrently the [governor-general of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor-general_of_India "Governor-general of India") and Calcutta was the [capital of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capital_of_India "Capital of India") until 1911.

The Bengal Presidency emerged from trading posts established in the [Bengal Subah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengal_Subah "Bengal Subah") of [Mughal Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mughal_Empire "Mughal Empire"), during the reign of Emperor [Jahangir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jahangir "Jahangir") in 1612. The East India Company (EIC), a British Indian monopoly with a royal charter, competed with other European companies to gain influence in Bengal. In 1757 and 1764, the company defeated the [Nawab of Bengal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nawab_of_Bengal "Nawab of Bengal"), who acted on Mughal sovereignty, at the [Battle of Plassey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Plassey "Battle of Plassey") and the [Battle of Buxar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Buxar "Battle of Buxar"), and Bengal came under British influence. In 1765, Emperor [Shah Alam II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shah_Alam_II "Shah Alam II") granted revenue rights over Bengal to the company and the judicial rights in 1793. After this, the Bengal province was later merged with the Presidency of Fort William but under the [suzerainty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suzerainty "Suzerainty") of the Emperor until 1835.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengal_Presidency#cite_note-8)

In 1836, the upper territories of the Bengal Presidency were organised into the Agra Division or [North-Western Provinces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North-Western_Provinces "North-Western Provinces") and administered by a lieutenant-governor within the Presidency. The lower territories were organised into the Bengal Division and put in charge of lieutenant-governor as well in 1853. The office of the governor of the Presidency was abolished and the Presidency existed as only a nominal entity under the dual government of the two lieutenant-governors at [Agra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agra "Agra") and Calcutta. The 1887, the Agra Division was separated from the Presidency and merged with the Oudh province, ending the dual government. In 1912, the governor was restored. In the early 20th century, Bengal emerged as a hotbed of the [Indian independence movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_independence_movement "Indian independence movement") and the [Bengali Renaissance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengali_Renaissance "Bengali Renaissance"),[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengal_Presidency#cite_note-9) as well as a center of education, politics, law, science and [the arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_arts "The arts"). It was home to the largest city in India and the second-largest city in the [British Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Empire "British Empire").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengal_Presidency#cite_note-10)

At its territorial height in the mid nineteenth century, the Bengal Presidency extended from the [Khyber Pass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khyber_Pass "Khyber Pass") to Singapore.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengal_Presidency#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengal_Presidency#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengal_Presidency#cite_note-WhiteBoard-13) In 1853, [the Punjab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punjab_Province_(1849%E2%80%931947) "Punjab Province (1849–1947)") was separated from the Presidency into a new province. In 1861, the [Saugor and Nerbudda Territories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saugor_and_Nerbudda_Territories "Saugor and Nerbudda Territories") of the North-Western Provinces (which was then a division of the Bengal Presidency) were separated from the Presidency and merged with the [Nagpur Province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nagpur_Province "Nagpur Province") to created the [Central Provinces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Provinces "Central Provinces"). In 1871, Ajmer and Merwara which were also administered as a part of the Northern States were separated from the Presidency to form the [Ajmer-Merwara State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ajmer-Merwara_Province "Ajmer-Merwara Province"). In 1874, [Assam State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assam_Province "Assam Province") was separated from Bengal.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengal_Presidency#cite_note-WhiteBoard-13) In 1862, [Burma division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Burma "British Burma") became a separate state.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengal_Presidency#cite_note-autogenerated2-14) In 1877, the North-Western Provinces were finally separated from Bengal and merged with Oudh which later created the Northern States or United Provinces. Thus, by 1877, the Bengal Presidency included only modern-day [Bihar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bihar "Bihar"), [Jharkhand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jharkhand "Jharkhand"), [Orissa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orissa "Orissa") and [Bengal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengal "Bengal"). In 1905, the [first partition of Bengal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partition_of_Bengal_(1905) "Partition of Bengal (1905)") resulted in the short-lived state of [Eastern Bengal and Assam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Bengal_and_Assam "Eastern Bengal and Assam") which existed alongside the Bengal Presidency. In 1912, the state was merged back with the Bengal Presidency while [Bihar and Orissa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bihar_and_Orissa "Bihar and Orissa") became a separate state.

In 1862, the [Bengal Legislative Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Bengal_Legislative_Council "British Bengal Legislative Council") became the first [legislature in British India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legislatures_of_British_India "Legislatures of British India") with native representation, after a petition from the [British Indian Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Indian_Association "British Indian Association") of Calcutta.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengal_Presidency#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengal_Presidency#cite_note-16) As part of efforts towards [home rule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Home_rule "Home rule"), the [Government of India Act 1935](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_India_Act_1935 "Government of India Act 1935") created a [bicameral legislature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bicameralism "Bicameralism"), with the [Bengal Legislative Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengal_Legislative_Assembly_(1937%E2%80%941947) "Bengal Legislative Assembly (1937—1947)") becoming the largest state assembly in India in 1937. The office of the [Prime Minister of Bengal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Bengal "Prime Minister of Bengal") was established as part of growing provincial autonomy. After the 1946 election, rising Hindu–Muslim divisions across India forced the Bengal Assembly to decide on partition, despite calls for a [United Bengal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Bengal "United Bengal"). The [Partition of British India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partition_of_British_India "Partition of British India") in 1947 resulted in the [second partition of Bengal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partition_of_Bengal_(1947) "Partition of Bengal (1947)") on religious grounds into [East Bengal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Bengal "East Bengal") (present-day Bangladesh) and [West Bengal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Bengal "West Bengal").

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bengal_Presidency&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

### Background

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bengal_Presidency&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Background")]

[![Image 40](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9d/Jahangir_of_India.jpg/250px-Jahangir_of_India.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Jahangir_of_India.jpg)

Jahangir first permitted the East India Company (EIC) to trade in Bengal

In 1599, a [royal charter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_charter "Royal charter") was granted by [Queen Elizabeth I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Elizabeth_I "Queen Elizabeth I") to allow the creation of a trading company in London for the purposes of trade with the East Indies. The governance of the company was placed in the hands of a governor and a 24-member Court of Directors. The corporation became known as the Honourable East India Company (HEIC). It became the most powerful corporation of its time, with control over half of [world trade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_trade "International trade"). [Edmund Burke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edmund_Burke "Edmund Burke") described the company as "a state in the guise of a merchant".[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengal_Presidency#cite_note-17) It was described as a "state within a state", and even "an empire within an empire".[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengal_Presidency#cite_note-18) The company was given a monopoly for British trade in the Indian Ocean.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengal_Presidency#cite_note-19)

In 1608, [Mughal Emperor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mughal_Emperor "Mughal Emperor")[Jahangir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jahangir "Jahangir") allowed the English East India Company to establish a small trading post on the west coast of India. It was followed in 1611 by a [factory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Factory_(trading_post) "Factory (trading post)") on the [Coromandel Coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coromandel_Coast "Coromandel Coast") in South India, and in 1612 the company joined other already established European trading companies to trade in the wealthy [Bengal Subah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengal_Subah "Bengal Subah") in the east.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengal_Presidency#cite_note-20) However, the power of the Mughal Empire declined from 1707, as the Nawab of Bengal in [Murshidabad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murshidabad "Murshidabad") became financially independent with the help of bankers such as the [Jagat Seth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jagat_Seth "Jagat Seth"). The Nawabs began entering into treaties with numerous European companies, including the [French East India Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_XIV's_East_India_Company "Louis XIV's East India Company"), the [Dutch East India Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_East_India_Company "Dutch East India Company"), and the [Danish East India Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danish_East_India_Company "Danish East India Company").

The Mughal court in Delhi was weakened by [Nader Shah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nader_Shah "Nader Shah")'s invasion from Persia (1739) and [Ahmed Shah Durrani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmed_Shah_Durrani "Ahmed Shah Durrani")'s invasion from Afghanistan (1761). While the Bengal Subah suffered a decade of [Maratha raids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maratha_invasions_of_Bengal "Maratha invasions of Bengal"), through bands of [Bargir-giri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bargi "Bargi") light cavalry, directed to pillage the territory, between 1741 and 1751.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengal_Presidency#cite_note-21) In 1742 the Company chooses to spend Rs. 25 thousand on the construction of a 3 km Maratha ditch around Calcutta, to protect its facilities from the raiders.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengal_Presidency#cite_note-22) The Nawab of Bengal later signed a peace treaty with the Marathas in 1751, and ceded [Orrisa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orrisa "Orrisa") and paid Rs. 1.2 million annually as the _[chauth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chauth "Chauth")_.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengal_Presidency#cite_note-oum-23) The Nawab of Bengal also paid Rs. 3.2 million to the Marathas, towards the arrears of _chauth_ for the preceding years.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengal_Presidency#cite_note-Mehta2005-24)

In June 1756, the company's factories at [Cossimbazar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cossimbazar "Cossimbazar")[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengal_Presidency#cite_note-25) and [Calcutta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siege_of_Calcutta "Siege of Calcutta") were besieged and captured by the forces of the Nawab of Bengal, with the company's goods, treasure and weapons seized.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengal_Presidency#cite_note-26)[_[unreliable source?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Reliable\_sources "Wikipedia:Reliable sources")_] Calcutta being renamed Alinagar in honour of the [Siraj ud-Daulah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siraj_ud-Daulah "Siraj ud-Daulah")'s predecessor. A Company force, led by Watson and [Robert Clive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Clive "Robert Clive"), recaptured Fort William in January 1757, with the Nawab, Siraj ud-Daulah, agreeing the [Treaty of Alinagar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Alinagar "Treaty of Alinagar"), reestablishing the company's right to trade in Bengal, and fortify Fort William. In parallel Robert Clive conspired with Jagat Seth, Omichand and [Mir Jafar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mir_Jafar "Mir Jafar") to install the latter on the musnud of Bengal, a plan that they would implement in June 1757.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengal_Presidency#cite_note-auto-27)

[![Image 41](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/87/Silver_Rupee_coins_of_the_Bengal_Presidency%2C_struck_in_the_name_of_Mughal_emperor_Shah_Alam_II%2C_photographed_by_Yogabrata_Chakraborty.jpg/250px-Silver_Rupee_coins_of_the_Bengal_Presidency%2C_struck_in_the_name_of_Mughal_emperor_Shah_Alam_II%2C_photographed_by_Yogabrata_Chakraborty.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Silver_Rupee_coins_of_the_Bengal_Presidency,_struck_in_the_name_of_Mughal_emperor_Shah_Alam_II,_photographed_by_Yogabrata_Chakraborty.jpg)

Silver Rupee coins of the Bengal Presidency, struck in the name of Mughal emperor [Shah Alam II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shah_Alam_II "Shah Alam II"); From top left: Rupee of George Saunders' issue of 1819 (Calcutta), Broad rimmed Rupee of Farrukhabad, Narrow rimmed Rupee of Farrukhabad, Rupee of Murshidabad from the 1780s, Rupee of Muhammadabad Benaras with the inverted mace symbol and rare fish mint mark.

The East India Company's victories at the [Battle of Plassey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Plassey "Battle of Plassey") (1757) and the [Battle of Buxar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Buxar "Battle of Buxar") (against the Nawabs of Bengal and [Oudh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nawab_of_Oudh "Nawab of Oudh") in 1764) led to the abolition of local rule (Nizamat) in Bengal in 1793. The Company gradually began to formally expand its territories across India and Southeast Asia.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengal_Presidency#cite_note-28) By the mid-19th century, the East India Company had become the paramount political and military power in the [Indian subcontinent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_subcontinent "Indian subcontinent"). Its territory was held in [trust](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trust_law "Trust law") for the [British Crown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Crown "The Crown").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengal_Presidency#cite_note-igi-ii-pp488-514-29) The company also issued coins in the name of the nominal Mughal Emperor (who was exiled in 1857).
